title: Community Flow registry - public GitHub repo where developers submit Flows for review
description:
UMBRELLA: MPI-560 (phase 7 - community Flow submissions). Created 2026-09-17 (Fabio).

TARGET: open the day Cubric Studio 2.0 ships, so developers can submit Flows to MPI for review from release day. Pulls the "1.7+ GitHub registry" idea in MPI-532 forward to 2.0.

SCOPE: a public GitHub repo where a developer submits a Flow package for MPI to review.
- README with the submission rules (package format = docs/flow-packages.md, allowed node packs = the developer kit lockfile).
- Issue / PR templates for a submission.
- CI that runs the Flow package linter (MPI-532 phase 4) on every submission.
- A public review checklist and public decisions (accept or decline, with the reason). The platform owner choosing what ships must be visible; transparency defuses it.
- Decide what an accepted entry becomes: a listing the next release bakes in as a Community Flows card that links to the developer's own page (MPI-780 open question 1 covers Library link tiles).
Advertising only: never a payment rail, no accounts, no checkout.

NEEDS FABIO: ANSWERED - see DECIDED below.

DEPENDS ON: MPI-532 (format, linter, docs) and the Flow developer kit card (lockfile + installer).

DECIDED 2026-09-19 (Fabio) - all four blocking answers are in, so this is no longer needs-decision:
1. REPO: MadPonyInteractive/cubric-flows-registry, PUBLIC. Fabio's go given. The "-registry" suffix is deliberate: c:\AI\Mpi\Cubric-Flows is ALREADY a local git repo of the same name holding MPI's two PAID packages with an All-rights-reserved LICENCE and NO remote. A public repo called cubric-flows is one mistyped push away from publishing the products.
2. LICENCE: MIT on the registry repo. NOT AGPL - the repo holds templates, CI and catalogue JSON, nothing served over a network, and an AGPL badge deters paid-Flow submitters for no benefit. Each Flow keeps its OWN licence: flow.json already carries a `licence` field (MPI's head-swap uses it) and services/userFlows.js never validates it, so CI can require it with ZERO changes to Vision. CI may run the AGPL linter - it checks out Cubric-Studio at the release tag and runs scripts/lint-flow-package.mjs; running an AGPL program relicenses nothing, and pinning to a tag is what makes the lint meaningful.
3. SUBMISSION SHAPE: a PR for BOTH lanes, and the registry is a CATALOGUE, never a file host (consistent with phase 7's "advertising only"). Every Flow gets one flows/<id>.json entry - mostly the manifest's own header fields.
   - FREE lane: the PR carries the metadata entry AND the package folder. CI lints it. Merge = listed and hosted; close = declined with a public reason.
   - PAID lane: the PR carries ONLY the metadata entry - Gumroad link, screenshots, required models, minAppVersion, licence, and a SHA256 of the package zip. The package never enters the public repo. The developer sends the zip privately; MPI runs the same linter locally; merging the metadata PR IS the public acceptance record.
   Why a PR and not an issue for the free lane: an issue cannot run a linter over attachments. A PR gets CI free and merge/close already means accept/decline - ONE workflow with ONE conditional (lint the package folder if present). The SHA256 is ~3 lines of CI and lets a buyer verify the zip they paid for is the one MPI reviewed.
4. PRIVATE CHANNEL for the paid lane: still needs an email address Fabio owns; left as a placeholder in the templates until he names one.

STILL UNBUILT: the repo does not exist yet. Plan this card before creating it - creating a public repo is the one step here that cannot be quietly undone.
